tool.name: DtedIndexBuild

param.name: input
param.dialogReference:
A DTED file (.dt0, .dt1, .dt2) or a folder of them: a delivery laid out as DTED/E006/N49.dt2, or any tree. Every file under the folder is found whatever the case of its name; files of another level than the one chosen are counted and skipped.

Browse to a DTED file and click OK, or choose a DTED layer of the map. Opening a file in the browse dialog lists its bands; a band chosen there (Band_1) is read as its file.
param.pythonReference: egmtrans dted-index build --from-dted PATH...: the DTED files or folders

param.name: dted_level
param.dialogReference: The level of the cells to index: only the files of that level are read, and an index describes one level. Left blank, the one level found under the input is taken; when several are found the build stops and reports their counts, so a folder that holds DTED1 and DTED2 cells gives one index per level. The level of a product profile stands in for a blank choice.

param.name: output
param.dialogReference: The index to write: a GeoPackage (.gpkg) or a GeoParquet file (.parquet, with its subregions in a sibling _subregions.parquet). Every column is written, NULL included, so the table can be reviewed and completed in a GIS; a NULL accuracy means NA, as the header said.

param.name: index_overrides
param.dialogReference:
Values written in every row, over what the headers hold: an index column and its value per row. Any column can be set except cell_id, dted_level and updated, which the build fills itself. A date takes YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD or today; an accuracy takes NA or whole meters; a blank clears an optional text column.

A row vertical_datum = E96 records the datum the cells will carry after a transform to EGM96, the datum EGMTrans writes; a row producer_code = <code> stamps the producer's own code, FIPS 10-4 country code first.

param.name: dted_profile
param.dialogReference: A TOML file of the header constants of the product, as the EGMTrans Tool takes it. Its values fill the text and date fields a header left blank (never an accuracy: a header's NA is a value), its level stands in for a blank DTED Level, and the validation after the build compares the rows with it.

tool.summary: Builds the DTED metadata index of a delivery from the headers of its DTED files: one row per one-degree cell, keyed by cell_id (N49E006), holding the security markings, references, edition, dates, producer, product specification, datum codes, accuracies and free text the UHL, DSI and ACC records carry, with the accuracy subregions of the ACC in a second layer and the file each row came from. The Index Overrides set a value in every row. After the write, the index is validated as a run would see it, and the messages say where each required header field comes from. The same index is built on the command line by "egmtrans dted-index build --out INDEX --from-dted PATH", which also takes --product, --update and the other sources.
tool.usage:
• The first messages count the files found by level. Only the files of the chosen level are read; with the level blank, the one level found is taken, and several levels found stop the build with their counts. One index describes one level.

  • A file that cannot be read (too short, no readable origin) is an error with no row; the index is still written for the other cells and the tool ends with an error. Two files of one cell at the level are an error naming both, and the cell gets no row.

  • A header value the index cannot hold (an edition of 00, a lowercase security code, a datum other than WGS84) is left NULL and reported once per problem with the cells concerned. The findings of the source headers (bytes that are not printable, a producer code without a country prefix) are summarized the same way and do not stop the build.

  • source_file is the path of the file relative to the folder given, so the index reads the same on another computer.

  • The validation findings and the supply lines follow: which required header fields the index, the profile or an override supplies, and which nothing supplies yet.

  • The index can be edited in ArcGIS Pro; run Validate DTED Index afterwards, then give it to the EGMTrans Tool as the DTED Metadata Index.
